subject: general
question: In a concave mirror, the object is placed between the pole and the focus point of the mirror. What is the nature of the image?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual and erect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed between the pole and the focus point of a concave mirror, the image formed is **virtual and erect**.
 
• The image is formed on the same side of the mirror as the object.
 
• The image is larger than the object (magnified).
 
• The virtual image cannot be projected onto a screen as it is formed by the apparent divergence of rays.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror that curves inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• It is also known as a converging mirror because it can converge light rays to a point.
 
 
 
• **Focus Point (F):**
 
 
• The point on the principal axis of a concave mirror where light rays parallel to the principal axis converge after reflection.
 
• The distance between the focus point and the mirror's surface is called the focal length.
 
 
 
• **Real Image:**
 
 
• An image formed by actual convergence of light rays that can be projected on a screen.
 
• Real images are always inverted in concave mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Image:**
 
 
• An image formed by the apparent divergence of light rays from a point.
 
• Virtual images are always erect and cannot be projected onto a screen.
